recent_articles.title: Mumbai, Maharashtra emerging as key hubs for global investment and clean energy partnerships, say diplomats - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Consul Generals** from **Australia** and **Finland** highlighted the growing investment opportunities in Mumbai and Maharashtra, emphasizing infrastructure development, clean energy, education, and technology sectors.  They praised Mumbai's transformation, citing projects like the Coastal Road and metro expansion as drivers of investor confidence. Both diplomats acknowledged challenges faced by foreign investors, including regulatory clarity and streamlined approval systems. Despite these challenges, they expressed optimism about Mumbai's long-term trajectory as a global economic hub.

recent_articles.title: KERC directs Escoms to give consumers 15 clear days to pay bills - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Karnataka Electricity Regulatory Commission (KERC)** has mandated that all electricity distribution companies provide consumers with a minimum of 15 days to pay their bills from the actual bill issuance date, not the scheduled billing date. The order, effective June 1st, requires all bills to clearly state the generation date and time, and mandates payment due dates be calculated accordingly.  The commission emphasized that late or extended billing cycles do not exempt Escoms from providing consumers with sufficient payment time.

recent_articles.title: Bowring Hospital wall collapse: Lokayukta probe finds major safety lapses - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A **Lokayukta** inquiry into the fatal wall collapse at the **Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital** in Shivajinagar, Karnataka, has revealed multiple structural and administrative failures. The investigation found that the wall was constructed beyond permissible height limits, had been damaged previously, and lacked proper drainage systems and retaining walls.  The inquiry also highlighted negligence by authorities who failed to monitor dangerous structures and encroachments. **Senior IAS and IPS officers**, officials from various departments, and hospital authorities appeared before the **Lokayukta** for questioning. The **Lokayukta** directed authorities to identify similar unsafe structures and take preventive measures.

recent_articles.title: Deepa Jewellers, Cotec Healthcare receive Sebi approval for IPOs - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Deepa Jewellers**, a Hyderabad-based company specializing in hallmarked gold jewelry processing and trading, plans to raise funds through an IPO consisting of a fresh issue and offer-for-sale. The IPO will include up to Rs 250 crore worth of shares from the company and up to 1.18 crore shares offered for sale by promoters **Ashish Agarwal** and **Seema Agarwal**.  **Cotec Healthcare**, a contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) serving pharmaceutical companies, also received Sebi approval for its IPO. The company manufactures formulations across various therapeutic segments and operates a manufacturing facility in Roorkee with an installed capacity of over 4 billion units.

recent_articles.title: Will TVK government take ‘firm stand’ on Mekedatu project, asks Palaniswami - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Edappadi K. Palaniswami**, general secretary of the **AIADMK**, questioned the **Tamil Nadu** government's ability to protect its interests in the **Mekedatu balancing reservoir project** on the Cauvery river, citing the reported support of the **Congress** party and concerns about potential power-sharing agreements.  **D.K. Shivakumar**, Karnataka’s Deputy Chief Minister, reportedly stated that Tamil Nadu had no right to object to the project, while **T.T.V. Dhinakaran**, founder of the **AMMK**, echoed these concerns.

recent_articles.title: States should be allowed to conduct CET for medical courses: CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Siddaramaiah** called for the decentralization of the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) and urged **States** to have the opportunity to conduct their own Common Entrance Tests (CET) for medical courses. He argued that education is a concurrent list subject, allowing states to independently administer entrance exams for professional courses within the federal system.

recent_articles.title: Fake call centres duping U.S. citizens busted in Bengaluru, man from Delhi, another from U.P. arrested - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Karnataka State Cyber Command** officials raided four fake call centers in Bengaluru, uncovering a sophisticated operation that defrauded U.S. citizens by impersonating a prominent American accounting firm. The accused, Prashanth and Akash, allegedly collected millions of rupees from victims through fake tax advice, license renewal services, and counterfeit software keys.  The investigation revealed the use of shell companies to launder money and a network of over 120 employees trained to deceive victims using US accents. **Pronab Mohanty**, Director General of Cyber Command, stated that further investigations will focus on tracing the money trail and identifying bank accounts used in the fraud.

recent_articles.title: Congress workers clash with police in Jaipur during stir against NEET-UG paper leak - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** party workers clashed with **police** in **Rajasthan** on Thursday during a protest against the NEET-UG exam paper leak.  Led by **State Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra**, the protesters demanded the resignation of **Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan** and the dissolution of the **National Testing Agency**. The demonstrators, carrying banners and placards, were forcibly dispersed using water cannons. Some protesters suffered minor injuries.

recent_articles.title: Suo motu case against top Karnataka officials after raids expose illegal sand mining in Bagalkot - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Lokayukta Police** in **Karnataka** have registered a suo motu case against several senior government officials, including the Director of the Mines and Geology Department in Bengaluru and the Bagalkot Deputy Commissioner, for alleged large-scale illegal sand mining in the Krishna river bed. The investigation followed complaints about rampant illegal mining activities in Bagalkot district and revealed indiscriminate excavation using heavy machinery in violation of environmental norms.  The **Lokayukta Police** conducted raids across Bagalkot district on May 21, seizing equipment and uncovering large quantities of illegally extracted sand.  Further investigations are underway to determine the extent of the illegal activity and hold those responsible accountable.

recent_articles.title: Mega merger incoming: Should you buy PFC, REC shares ahead of merger? Here's what analysts say - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nirmala Sitharaman**, the **Union Finance Minister**, announced plans to restructure **Power Finance Corporation (PFC)** and **Rural Electrification Corporation (REC)** for streamlined operations. The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved a proposal where PFC acquired 52.63% of the government's holding in REC, consolidating them into a single balance sheet.  Analysts suggest investors consider staggered exposure to PFC and REC as the merger process is subject to regulatory approvals and structural adjustments. While PFC offers better visibility due to its parent status, REC presents a merger-arbitrage opportunity with higher event risk depending on the swap ratio.

recent_articles.title: Stray dog euthanasia: Bengaluru examining legally permissible options for ‘rabid, ill, or aggressive dogs’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Bengaluru’s corporations** are grappling with the Supreme Court's ruling that allows for euthanasia of "rabid, incurably ill or demonstrably dangerous" dogs. The court emphasized qualified veterinary assessments and adherence to existing animal welfare laws.  However, a lack of clear guidelines on aggression levels has raised concerns about potential misuse by civic officials. Animal rights activist Arun Prasad warns this could lead to unnecessary dog killings. Meanwhile, Nevina Kamath, a co-petitioner in a previous case regarding stray dog euthanasia, plans to file a review petition against the new ruling.

recent_articles.title: PM busy handing out candies in Italy amid economic storm at home, says Congress - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** president Mallikarjun Kharge and **Rahul Gandhi** criticized the **Narendra Modi** government's economic policies, accusing it of prioritizing publicity over addressing rising inflation, unemployment, and weakening economic indicators.  **Kharge** highlighted the increase in average debt per Indian and wealth concentration among billionaires, while **Gandhi** criticized the Prime Minister's focus on foreign trips during a time of economic distress. Congress officials also pointed to the rupee's decline, falling foreign exchange reserves, and large investor outflows as evidence of government mismanagement.

recent_articles.title: Bidadi township: Deve Gowda announces stir against project; DKS hits back - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **H.D. Deve Gowda**, former Prime Minister, launched a campaign against the proposed Bidadi township project, claiming it targets fertile agricultural land and is driven by a "land business." He accused the **Siddaramaiah** government of facilitating this project under the guise of urban development, drawing parallels with previous satellite township projects that were withdrawn due to public opposition. **D.K. Shivakumar**, Deputy Chief Minister, countered Gowda's accusations, alleging that the Kumaraswamy family amassed wealth through real estate dealings and initiated similar projects in the past.

recent_articles.title: NEET paper leak row: Congress demands resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** leaders demanded the resignation of **Dharmendra Pradhan**, the **Union Education Minister**, over the NEET-UG paper leak scandal.  They accused the government of a "money-making racket" involving people linked to the ruling establishment and claimed that the incident had caused immense trauma for 22 lakh students. **Rahul Gandhi** called for the Prime Minister's intervention, while **Mallikarjun Kharge**, the Congress president, alleged that the Modi government was undermining student credibility through repeated paper leaks.  **Jairam Ramesh**, a Congress general secretary, criticized the government's lack of action and incompetence in addressing exam reforms.

recent_articles.title: Medical Education Minister demands court-monitored probe into NEET paper leak - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Karnataka Medical Education Minister Sharan Prakash Patil** criticized the ongoing investigation into the NEET question paper leak, calling for a court-monitored probe. He expressed concerns that the **Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)**'s current investigation lacked transparency and confidence, suggesting powerful individuals were involved in orchestrating the scandal to manipulate MBBS seat sales.

recent_articles.title: BJP protests State government’s decision to withdraw uniform rule in educational institutions - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **BJP** district unit members protested against the **State government's** decision to withdraw uniform regulations in educational institutions, arguing that it would disrupt discipline and academic atmosphere. The protesters, including former MP Umesh Jadhav and BJP leaders Baburao Chavan, Sudha Halkai, Chandrakant Patil, and Ashok Bagli, demanded intervention from the Governor to retain the policy. They claimed uniforms promote secular values and reduce socioeconomic disparities among students.

recent_articles.title: Submerged temple emerges as Bhavanisagar Dam level drops - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Bhavanisagar Dam**'s water level dropping to 59 ft. has revealed the dilapidated **Sri Madhava Perumal Temple**, which was submerged during construction in the 1940s and 1950s.  A study of inscriptions on the temple premises found it to be located at the confluence of the Bhavani and Moyar rivers, once a significant trade route connecting Kongu with Karnataka and Kerala. The site is believed to have been ruled by the Hoysalas and served as the location for a fort built by **Madhava Perumal Dhandanayaka**, a general appointed by King Veera Ballala III.  The temple was last visible in 2024 when the water level dropped, and fishermen report that portions of the structure become visible again at lower water levels.
